newsitem.title: EGYPT: Israel president in Egypt on "save peace" mission.
newsitem.headline: Israel president in Egypt on "save peace" mission.

text.p: Israeli President Ezer Weizman arrived in Egypt on Monday to try to mend the damage Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's hardline policies have inflicted on the Jewish state's relations with its Arab neighbours.

Weizman will hold talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak, whose country is the most influential Arab state. Mubarak has said Egyptians are furious with Netanyahu and are calling for a boycott of the Jewish state.

Weizman, whose office is by law largely ceremonial, has said his role in Egypt would be to "heal certain splits, which everyone sees, with the largest Arab country, and I think we can find a number of directions for improved relations."

Egypt, which in 1979 became the first Arab state to make peace with the Jewish state, has repeatedly called on Netanyahu to honour peace pledges signed with the Palestinians. The Israeli prime minister has been trying to renegotiate them.
Mubarak told reporters on Saturday he had told Netanyahu he would not meet him unless Israeli troops withdrew from the West Bank town of Hebron as stipulated in previous agreements.
The Egyptian leader even refused to attend an emergency summit in Washington earlier this month because he did not believe Netanyahu would change his position.
Weizman was a key architect of the Camp David peace accords signed by Egypt and Israel in 1978.
